chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Jamīl, from Samāʿah, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman who had prayed two rakʿahs of ẓuhr, then menstruation began for her while she was sitting. He said: “She rises from her place of prayer and does not make up those two rakʿahs.”

key_terms.تَقْضِي: she makes up or performs as qaḍāʾ

ai.seo_question: If a woman begins menstruating in the middle of ẓuhr prayer, does she have to make up the rakʿahs she prayed?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a woman whose menstruation begins during the ẓuhr prayer after completing two rakʿahs. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that she should leave her place of prayer and is not required to make up the two rakʿahs already prayed in that interrupted state.
